reliability.decision_rule_predeclared: every counter equal or better at 2w than 1w on the SAME workload, else regression
reliability.defect_detail: run_3 (2 workers): B2_REUSE launched TWICE (launch file shows pid 49399 window [1789845903.526, 1789845909.66] then pid 49717 window [1789845909.763, 1789845915.83] — sequential, not concurrent), 19x beta:STALE_GENERATION_WRITE_BLOCKED cycles, final mission state PASS with lease_generation=2 (B1 stayed 1), wall 20.137s (+36.1% vs the canonical 2w median — 20.137/14.796; corrected 2026-09-20 per reviewer remark 3, the previously published +34% matched only the slowest canonical run 15.004 at +34.2%), still settled 4/4. Fencing held (no double settlement, no concurrent same-mission engines) but the duplicate launch wasted a full 6s engine run and spun blocked polls.
reliability.defect_mechanism: intra-portfolio parallel advances: in the window between the engine process EXITING and its settlement being written, the worker heartbeat is gone, so a sibling advance on the same project legitimately sees 'no live worker + not settled' and re-dispatches the mission (new lease generation); the first advance's settlement is then refused as stale generation until the second attempt settles. Impossible at MAX_WORKERS=1 (no sibling dispatcher exists).
reliability.additional_disclosure: one further occurrence with the same signature (B2 launches=2, stale-generation storm, wall 21.094s) was observed in a first benchmark execution whose raw files were replaced by the final instrumentation upgrade; it is disclosed here as an observation and NOT counted in the pooled citable sample (rate would be 2/12).
reliability.regression_verdict: REGRESSED_AT_2W: single-launch-per-mission holds 11/11 at 1 worker vs 10/11 at 2 workers (citable files; 10/12 counting the disclosed occurrence). Reliability is NOT non-regressed.
